topic: coordinate plane, line plots and patterns: order and scale mistakes

traps.desc: decided the two points must be the same place because they are made from the same two numbers
counted only the sideways move and forgot the up-and-down move
answered with the first number of the pair, which is the across value, when the up value was asked for
repeated the height printed under the marks instead of counting the marks stacked above it
answered with how many marks stand in the tallest stack instead of the height that stack sits above
counted how many different heights are marked on the line instead of how many plants were measured
put the term from the second pattern in the first slot of the pair
put the term from the first pattern in the second slot of the pair

problems.desc: Open task: plot and label (6,2) and (2,6) on the grid, then explain in one or two sentences why they are different points even though they use the same two numbers, and give a way to remember which number goes first. Read by hand. Full credit needs both points plotted correctly and clearly labelled; a sentence saying the first number counts across from the origin and the second counts up, so swapping them lands somewhere else; and a memory aid such as 'along the hall, then up the stairs' or 'x comes before y in the alphabet'.
